title: Staggered rollback & scope-triage playbook for combined API/Console/Runtime release train
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Create a single operational playbook that defines staggered rollback windows and a cross-product scope-triage matrix for coordinated launches across Redwood API, Console, and Runtime. Scope: milestone dates, cut criteria by subsystem, rollback windows, decision authority, and comms templates. Exclusions: deep technical runbooks for kernel-level rollbacks (those remain ENG owned), on-prem upgrade sequences are out of scope for this ticket and tracked separately. Constraints: maintain minimum Hosted API uptime SLA during rollout; Dedicated customers must receive 48h pre-notice for any disruptive cut. The playbook should surface measurable signals (SLOs, error budget, perf regressions) and explicit thresholds for automated and manual cut decisions.
acceptance_criteria: A consolidated scope-triage matrix that maps features to release lanes (API, Console, Runtime) and identifies must-cut vs deferred components
Clearly defined cut criteria for each lane: SLO thresholds, perf regression tolerances, customer-facing bug categories, and security blockers
A documented staggered rollback schedule (canary -> partial -> full) with owners, decision authority, and comms templates
Integration points listed for Console release notes, API changelog, and Runtime release blog; owner for each asset assigned
Playbook reviewed and sign-off captured from Eng Lead, SRE, PM, and Design prior to milestone freeze

review_feedback: Engineering review: prefer shorter canary for config flags but accept 72h for behavioral changes; require runbook link for quick rollback instructions.
SRE review: want two-level automated thresholds (soft warn at 40% budget, hard stop at 20%); request playbook include post-rollback RCA template.
Design review: emphasized clarity in console banners and rollback CTAs; suggested color and wording standards for different severity levels.
Legal/privacy: telemetry or audit-related changes must be blocked from release until compliance sign-off; flagged as non-negotiable cut criteria.
Support/GTM: requested ready-made customer comms for VIP Dedicated accounts, with T+1 engineer contact path during canary windows.
notes: Guiding principle: prioritize user-facing stability over feature completeness. When in doubt, prefer scope deferment to avoid wide blast radius. For Dedicated customers we maintain a stricter bar and will run a parallel dry-run deployment in a reserved pool before cut. Record all decisions in the decision table with timestamp and approvers.
